text.p: Italian bond futures eased throughout the day taking their direction from lower German bunds and U.S. Treasuries, while concern over EMU starting on time continued to weigh on market sentiment, dealers said.

Futures had briefly started firmer early but then slipped into the downward trend seen on Tuesday with most global markets awaiting the second leg of Fed chairman Alan Greenspan's Humphrey-Hawkins testimony later today.
"It was a day for sellers, most other markets were lower, the lira stayed weak so there was little reason to jump in and buy," said one LIFFE trader.

Dealers said that the BTP market was very cautious awaiting German February employment figures on Thursday and February U.S. jobs data on Friday. Concern over EMU being delayed continued to worry the Italian market, they added.

The bund market took little support after German finance minister Theo Waigel said his country can qualify for EMU if unemployment falls by the summer. Flat fourth quarter 1996 German GDP data depressed the bund market, dealers added.
"A combination of a weak German picture, the slide in T-bonds and Greenspan put most of the markets on a backward footing," said the LIFFE trader.
Dealers said little support came from currencies with the dollar steady despite renewed talk of a possible delay in EMU while the lira was largely unchanged at lower levels.
